content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question about SD card usage and the working hours counter function block: Normally, if the system is functioning correctly, [product_name] does not read the program from the SD card but operates from internal memory, which enables the working hours to be tracked. However, if [product_name] experiences a failure and subsequently reloads the program from the SD card, the working hours (OT) are reset, correct? To restore the correct working hours, do you need to manually enter the previous value (assuming you know it) into the 'Start time for OT' and then re-download to [product_name]? Is this the only available method?

This brings up a question for me: Why do you store the program on the SD card at all? The memory in [product_name] is flash-based and non-volatile, so the program remains intact unless it is deleted or changed.
Alright, but [company_name] included SD card support for a reason—what is its purpose?

It’s definitely not because the flash program memory loses its content. The SD card was added starting with [version_no] to enable longer-term data logging. Another use: You can save a program (or program change) in a special format on the SD card, send it to your customer, and have them insert it into their [product_name]. When they start [product_name], the new or updated program is automatically transferred from the card. The SD card is then removed. Also, since [version_no], using the SD card is required if you want extended web server access—the project for this must be stored on the SD card.

In addition to what [user_name] mentioned: I use the SD card as a working backup in case users modify parameters like timers and forget the original settings (this happens often). Then I simply ask them to reboot and use the SD card version so everything is restored to the intended setup.

This approach only works if (depending on the [product_name] version) the SD card’s program is write-protected. As of [version_no], parameter changes can be saved to an SD card during runtime. [IMAGE] Sales and Delivery Release for [product_name] BM [article_no] and [product_name] [version_no]

@[user_name], thanks for your update. I haven’t used [article_no] on these projects yet, and your input will help me avoid issues in the future. Up to now, my own workaround has proven effective for resolving problems caused by some users. I appreciate this forum, as I learn something new every day.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed SD card interactions with the working hours counter in [product_name] hardware. They expressed uncertainty about how the working hours are managed when a program is reloaded from an SD card and highlighted concerns about parameter persistence during recovery processes. Discussions also covered SD card usage for backup, enabling additional web server functionality, and parameter storage, showing mixed understanding about its roles.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the working hours counter value not to reset when the program is reloaded from the SD card and are looking for an automated method to restore correct working hours, rather than relying on manual input.
